channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: MIA Watchlist: Track whether the US-Iran port and Red Sea blockades widen, Friday's expiry of the 10% tariff baseline and new ~60-country duties, Europe's chemical trajectory, US-China tech decoupling, and whether Typhoon Hongxia forms.
item.description:
• US–Iran and the Red Sea: whether the two-carrier port blockade and the Houthi Red Sea blockade widen the war, and where Brent settles after the five-week-high spike toward USD 91 and pullback below USD 89.
  • Friday tariff cliff: the expiry of the 10% baseline and the shape of the new 10–12.5% duties on ~60 countries, plus retaliation risk and the generic-drug tariff timeline to 2028.
  • Europe's chemical trajectory: whether the German output recovery holds, how the ETS revision is finalised after FEIQUE's objections, and further signals on energy costs and capacity.
  • US–China tech decoupling: whether Washington adds Chinese AI labs to the Entity List and whether Beijing imposes AI and semiconductor export controls, set against the reopened EU–China dialogue (see other insight in this alert).
  • Weather and harvests: whether Typhoon Hongxia forms and strikes Taiwan, the scale of Vietnam flood recovery, and how heatwaves and wildfires feed agricultural losses and food-price pressure into H2.

item.title: Typhoon Bawi dumped over 600mm on Taiwan's Miaoli (TWD 15.83m in farm losses) with Typhoon Hongxia possibly forming by Friday, northern Vietnam floods caused ~443bn dong in damage and six deaths, and Canadian wildfires cut logging supply.
item.description:
This clusters several new climate-driven disruptions into one logistics-and-supply picture. In Taiwan, Typhoon Bawi brought more than 600mm of rain to Miaoli, triggering 91 disaster reports, multiple road and farm-road collapses and TWD 15.83m in agricultural losses, while forecasters warn a tropical disturbance could strengthen into Typhoon Hongxia — the year's 12th — and reach the region by Friday or Saturday. In northern Vietnam, landslides and floods caused an estimated 443bn dong in damage, six deaths, and hit over 408ha of crops and 250-plus homes, with mountainous Lai Chau hardest hit. In Canada, ongoing wildfires have cut logging supply in a forest sector that contributes over CAD 20bn and employs about 200,000 people, and a separate UK moorland blaze from a car crash closed a key road. Research cited this week also underlined that wildfire smoke causes more inflammation and tissue damage than ordinary air pollution, compounding the health and operating costs of recurring fires.

Industry Impact

The channels for ACS are logistics, raw materials and operating conditions. Typhoons and floods disrupt manufacturing, construction and transport in electronics- and agriculture-heavy Asian economies, delaying projects that consume coatings and sealants and interrupting component flows. Wildfire-driven timber-supply losses raise costs and volatility for wood-based construction and furniture inputs, while recurring smoke events add worker-safety and site-operating costs in North America. Build climate resilience and modal flexibility into regional logistics planning, and treat recurring extreme-weather disruption as a budgeted operating risk rather than an exceptional event.

Commercial Times | Chinatimes | The Straits Times | BNN Bloomberg | Daily Sabah

item.title: China's Wang Yi told a European Parliament delegation that China is "a partner, not a problem" and urged balanced trade, as a scholar predicted localized frictions not a full trade war, while 67.9% of goods blocked at EU borders in 2025 came from China.
item.description:
This is a new diplomatic overture that follows, and softens, the harder Franco-German line reported in recent alerts. In Beijing, Wang Yi met a delegation led by European Parliament foreign-affairs chair David McAllister, calling for a dynamic, long-term balancing of EU–China trade and urging Europe to adopt "rational and objective" perceptions of China; the Foreign Ministry separately rejected Macron and Merz's "existential threat" framing, insisting China is part of the solution to Europe's difficulties. A Beijing Foreign Studies University professor argued a full-scale EU–China trade war is unlikely, but that localized frictions will grow in frequency and intensity as the EU and UK elevate national-security considerations across economic policy. The friction is visible in the data: the European Commission's customs report found 67.9% of goods blocked at EU borders for non-compliance or serious risk in 2025 originated from China — down from a 74.9% peak in 2024 but well above 2022–23 levels.

Industry Impact

For ACS producers exposed to China-linked supply chains and customers, a reopened dialogue track is a hedge against the decoupling scenarios dominating the alert's trade stories. Renewed EU–China engagement could stabilise some chemical and materials flows and slow the pace of new barriers. But the border-block data and the "localized frictions" forecast show the underlying tension is intensifying, not resolving, so this is fragile de-escalation rather than a turning point. Keep contingency planning for renewed EU–China friction, and watch whether the parliamentary engagement translates into concrete relief on tariffs, standards or market access.

China Daily | Global Times | Chinatimes | Il Sole 24 Ore

item.title: Indonesia grew 5.61% in Q1 with inflation near target, Singapore's non-oil domestic exports rose 20.7% in June for a tenth straight month, and Vietnam's IPO market rebounded, even as the IMF flagged oil and monsoon risks to India.
item.description:
Against a turbulent global backdrop, Southeast Asia and India show relative strength. Indonesia's Q1 GDP grew 5.61%, with growth expected to hold and inflation inside the 2.5% ±1% target, though the H1 budget deficit widened to IDR 196.5tn (0.76% of GDP). Singapore's non-oil domestic exports expanded 20.7% year-on-year in June, a tenth consecutive month of growth, buoyed by electronics — though analysts caution non-electronics exports may weaken in H2 as AI-investment momentum cools. Vietnam's IPO market staged an "impressive recovery" per Deloitte, with four listings in H1 after none a year earlier. India is the qualified case: the IMF slightly adjusted its 2026/27 forecasts, warning that a widening Middle East war lifting oil prices and an El Niño-weakened monsoon are the biggest downside risks, given India imports nearly 80% of its oil — even as New Delhi targets a 10% share of global merchandise exports by 2047, up from 1.8% in 2024.

Industry Impact

These markets are increasingly important growth and manufacturing bases for ACS. Resilient GDP, strong electronics exports and recovering capital markets support demand for adhesives, coatings and sealants in construction, electronics and consumer goods, and reinforce ASEAN's role as a supply-chain diversification destination. But the reliance on electronics and exposure to oil and weather risk (India in particular) make the strength conditional on the same war-energy variables running through this alert. Weigh serving these markets through local production versus exports, and track electronics-export momentum and oil-price transmission as the near-term signals for regional ACS demand.

Antara News | Singapore Business Review | Vietnam Economic Times | The Economic Times | Business Standard

item.title: Anduril and Archer unveiled the autonomous "Thunder" attack drone at Farnborough and Saab and Embraer agreed to build 20 more Gripens in Brazil, while a wave of eVTOL deals spanned the UK, Saudi Arabia, Canada and Taiwan.
item.description:
The airshow's second-half theme is autonomy and new aircraft categories rather than the traditional widebody contest. Anduril and Archer publicly showed "Thunder", positioned as a US Army fifth-class large UAV able to team with manned aircraft — a sign of how autonomous systems are moving to the centre of procurement. Saab and Embraer signed a Heads of Agreement to build 20 additional Gripens at Embraer's Brazilian complex to meet global demand, deepening a cross-border production partnership. Commercial rivalry resurfaced as Boeing asked the US government to press the EU for transparency over a EUR 3bn loan package to Airbus, reviving subsidy tensions as Airbus eyes a new aircraft around 2030. The clearest growth signal was in advanced air mobility: the UK government took interest in a military variant of Vertical Aerospace's eVTOL (and added a GBP 10m grant), Saudi Arabia's GACA signed an AAM MoU with Vertical, Canada's Horizon Aircraft secured a USD 600m LOI for up to 100 hybrid-electric VTOLs, and SkyDrive, ITRI and 7A Drones agreed to prepare eVTOL medevac services in Taiwan.

Industry Impact

Aerospace and defence are high-value ACS end-markets — structural adhesives, sealants and specialty coatings are integral to airframes, engines, drones and eVTOL platforms, and are typically high-margin and specification-locked. The shift toward autonomous systems and electric air mobility opens new, fast-growing materials segments (lightweight structures, battery and electronics encapsulation) alongside the established defence build-out. Prioritise qualification for drone and eVTOL platforms as well as traditional airframes, and track which programmes and primes secure orders to align material supply with the most durable demand.

Chinatimes | MarketScreener | MarketScreener | The Guardian | Asharq Al-Awsat

item.title: France cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.7% as repeated heatwaves hit output, UK unemployment held at 4.9% with vacancies down nearly 50% from 2022, and Fitch projected developed-economy government debt at a record USD 75.8tn — 104% of GDP.
item.description:
Several economic-performance signals point to a softening, fiscally strained Europe. France lowered its 2026 GDP forecast from 0.9% to 0.7%, citing slowing activity and three heatwaves that threaten agriculture, while weighing cuts to EDF's preferential energy tariff amid union strikes. In the UK, the first data under new Prime Minister Burnham showed unemployment steady at 4.9% (just below the 5% expected) but a weak labour market — vacancies down almost 50% from their 2022 peak to 712,000, wage growth easing to 3.4% and youth unemployment edging up. The macro overhang is debt: Fitch expects developed-economy government debt to rise USD 4.2tn this year to a record USD 75.8tn, or 104% of GDP, driven by persistent deficits, rising spending and geopolitical tension. JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon reinforced the caution, warning that investors are underestimating geopolitical and fiscal risks and that he would not buy stocks or long-dated Treasurys at current prices.

Industry Impact

For ACS producers this is the demand-and-financing backdrop for the core European market: sub-1% French growth and a cooling UK labour market point to soft construction and manufacturing demand, while record sovereign debt raises the risk of higher-for-longer rates and future fiscal tightening that would weigh further on activity. Heatwave-driven agricultural losses also feed input and demand volatility in agriculture-linked coatings and packaging. Plan European volumes conservatively, favour pricing discipline and cash efficiency over volume assumptions, and treat sovereign-debt and rate risk as a live constraint on H2 demand.

Les Echos | The Guardian | MarketScreener | MarketScreener | The Standard

item.title: China's urban youth unemployment reached 14.9% in June — the highest for the month since students were excluded from the sample — and an ANZ economist expects it to approach 20% as a record 12.7 million graduates enter the workforce amid AI displacement.
item.description:
The new detail this run is the labour-market strain beneath the headline high-tech growth. June joblessness for those aged 16–24 hit 14.9% and is forecast to near 20% in the coming two months, with an oversupply of labour intensified by a record 12.7 million graduates (up almost 4%) and AI beginning to displace entry-level roles. The demand picture is similarly soft: used-car transactions (8.095 million in the first five months) nearly matched new-car sales (8.148 million) for the first time, a sign of cautious consumers trading down. There are stabilisation signals too — first-tier city home prices rose month-on-month for a fourth straight month (new homes +0.1–0.2%, existing +0.3–0.4%), and foreign investment in Shenzhen's Qianhai zone jumped 102.9% to CNY 25.01bn in H1. On energy, Beijing lifted refined-fuel export restrictions in July but kept tight controls, reserving most quotas for state refiners and requiring inventories above the end-February mark.

Industry Impact

For ACS producers this is a demand-side caution to set against China's high-tech manufacturing momentum. Rising youth unemployment and consumers trading down point to softer discretionary and construction-linked demand — a headwind for coatings and materials tied to property, autos and consumer goods — even as electronics and equipment demand holds up. The tentative property-price stabilisation is worth watching as a leading indicator for construction-chemical volumes. Weight China planning toward high-tech and equipment end-markets over consumer- and property-exposed segments, and watch labour and housing data for signs the slowdown is spreading.

The Straits Times | Lianhe Zaobao | Xinhua | China Economic Net | South China Morning Post

item.title: PM Sanae Takaichi's cabinet approved its first fiscal blueprint, prioritising aggressive strategic spending with no clear consolidation path, as Japan posted a JPY 1.01tn H1 trade deficit driven partly by Middle East supply disruption.
item.description:
This is a new policy direction for a priority economy. The guidelines designate FY2027 as "the first year of responsible and proactive" spending, steering money toward strategic sectors while conspicuously omitting a commitment to fiscal consolidation — a notable tonal shift under Takaichi. A parallel regional strategy through FY2030 combines national industrial policy with locally developed programmes, building clusters around 17 priority areas to strengthen regional economies. The fiscal room is tightening: Japan's H1 trade deficit reached JPY 1.01tn as imports rose 10.7% to JPY 61.67tn and exports 13.7% to JPY 60.66tn, with Middle East crude imports down 26.4% on Hormuz disruption and the June deficit widening to JPY 406.9bn. The combination — expansionary fiscal intent against a widening external deficit and war-driven energy costs — sets up a test of whether targeted spending can lift growth without straining Japan's finances.

Industry Impact

Japan is a major manufacturing and chemical economy and an important ACS market, so an aggressive-spending, industrial-cluster strategy could support demand in construction, electronics and advanced manufacturing where adhesives, coatings and sealants are used. But the widening trade deficit and Middle East energy exposure underline the same feedstock and cost risks running through this alert (see other insight in this alert). Track which strategic sectors and regional clusters draw the new spending for materials-demand signals, and watch the yen and energy-cost path as inputs to Japanese industrial competitiveness.

Japan Today | Xinhua | The Mainichi | The Nation

item.title: US automakers are racing to purge Chinese connected-car hardware ahead of a federal ban, as the IEA warned China's rare-earth and graphite export controls expose a major EV supply-chain vulnerability and global EV sales growth slowed to 2% in H1.
item.description:
Several threads point the same way — a forced, security-driven reconfiguration of the auto supply chain. Ahead of a US rule banning Chinese connected-car software and hardware in American vehicles by decade-end, start-up Eagle Wireless is scaling from about 140 staff toward a planned 1,000, an early staging ground for replacing Chinese vehicle electronics. The IEA warned that China's proposed rare-earth and graphite export controls have exposed a major weakness in the global EV supply chain, with a large share of manufacturing outside China at risk across autos, tech, defence and energy. The demand backdrop is cooling and uneven: global EV sales rose just 2% year-on-year to 9.6 million units through June, but with Europe up 31% in June (~530,000), China's domestic market down 11% (~1 million) and North America down 13% (130,000). Politics is intruding too — Hungary opened an investigation into a BYD investment deal after a former foreign minister took a top job at the carmaker.

Industry Impact

Automotive is a core ACS end-market, so a security-driven decoupling reshapes where automotive adhesives, coatings and sealants demand sits and which suppliers qualify. Purging Chinese hardware opens opportunities for non-Chinese component and materials suppliers, but rare-earth and graphite controls threaten the inputs behind EV motors, batteries and electronics. The regional split — European EV strength against Chinese and North American softness — argues for geographically differentiated planning. Map critical-mineral exposure in automotive applications, position to serve reshored non-Chinese supply chains, and track the connected-car rule and Chinese export controls as the key variables.

BNN Bloomberg | Business Standard | Alliance for Automotive Innovation | Daily Sabah

item.title: Taiwan's June export orders hit a record USD 95.26bn, up 59.4% year-on-year and well above the 49.5% forecast, as three think tanks now project 2026 growth above 10% and Fitch sees 9.4% — all driven by AI-related semiconductor and electronics demand.
item.description:
This is a fresh set of standout economic figures for a critical electronics hub. Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs reported a 17th consecutive month of order growth, with information-and-communication and electronic-product orders up 81.9% and 79.9% respectively and US orders surging 83.6% to USD 38.66bn; first-half orders reached USD 504.1bn (+50.9%). The macro read-through is exceptional: the government's earlier 9.6% growth forecast may be exceeded, Academia Sinica sees above 10%, three major think tanks (CIER, TIER and a third) now project double-digit growth, and Fitch expects 9.4% in 2026 before a slowdown to 4.8% and 4.5% in 2027–28. President Lai framed Taiwan as a core node of the AI-era infrastructure, and NVIDIA's Jensen Huang called the island's supply chain the world's most advanced electronics manufacturing centre, not merely low-cost — as Wistron and NVIDIA partner to take AI-driven advanced manufacturing and industrial digital twins to the US.

Industry Impact

Semiconductors and advanced electronics are high-value ACS end-markets — specialty adhesives, encapsulants and coatings are integral to chip packaging, assembly and devices — so Taiwan's AI-fuelled surge sustains demand for electronics-grade materials and the qualification-locked supply that goes with them. The concentration of AI-hardware demand in Taiwan's ecosystem also signals where materials growth and capacity investment will cluster. Prioritise qualification into Taiwan's advanced-electronics supply chain and the AI-hardware build-out, while noting Fitch's projected 2027–28 deceleration as a reminder the current pace is cyclically extraordinary.

Lianhe Zaobao | Handelsblatt | Commercial Times | Chinatimes | Commercial Times

item.title: After Chinese models erased America's AI lead, the Commerce Department is reportedly weighing adding top Chinese AI labs to its Entity List, which would bar US firms from their software, while China mulls export controls on AI and chip technology.
item.description:
This is a new front opening in the technology war. According to reporting cited by industry insiders, the administration is weighing a "slower and more durable" pressure strategy: adding leading Chinese AI labs to the export-control Entity List, which would make it illegal for US companies to host or use their models, creating regulatory risk around any American use of Chinese AI. The move follows the shock of open-source Chinese models topping global benchmarks, and it has split the US AI industry — some argue restrictions protect domestic leaders, others that they cut off the cheapest frontier tools. The mirror-image response is forming in Beijing, where regulators are considering tightening export controls on AI and semiconductor technologies — turning China's own advances into potential leverage. Together the two moves point toward a bifurcating global AI stack, with Western and Chinese model ecosystems increasingly walled off from each other.

Industry Impact

The direct ACS exposure is limited, but the second-order effects are strategic. A bifurcating AI and semiconductor landscape raises the odds of renewed tech-tied tariff or export-control escalation that disrupts chemical and materials supply chains, and it shapes which AI tools are available for manufacturing and process optimisation on each side of the divide. Chinese export controls on AI and chips also risk spilling into the critical-minerals and specialty-materials domain that underpins electronics-grade adhesives and coatings. Track how far the Entity-List and Chinese export-control moves go, and keep contingency scenarios for a widening tech-and-materials decoupling.

The Times of India | Commercial Times | The Financial Times

item.title: German chemical output has risen since January after years of crisis, though still ~20% below 2021, even as Spain's FEIQUE warned the EU's ETS revision risks shrinking industry, not emissions, amid high energy costs and global competition.
item.description:
This is the most directly ACS-relevant cluster in the alert, and its two sides are the delta. On the upside, the NZZ Industry Monitor shows German chemical output — nearly EUR 160bn of sales in 2025, about 7% of industrial sales and 342,000 jobs — recovering month by month, a rare bright spot against the sector's deindustrialisation narrative, though the rebound is from a low base and structural problems persist. The counterweight is policy risk: FEIQUE said the Commission's ETS proposal fails to address rising near-term CO₂ costs or the structural barriers to decarbonisation, and pressed Brussels (in a meeting with Vice-President Ribera) for competitive electricity prices and stronger carbon-leakage protection. The backdrop remains harsh — the IW estimates Germany lost around 400,000 industrial jobs between 2019 and 2025, blaming China's trade policy, lost cheap Russian energy and US tariffs — while a DECHEMA study maps the long shift of basic chemicals off fossil naphtha and gas toward CO₂ and biogenic carbon sources.

Industry Impact

Chemicals are the feedstock base for adhesives, coatings and sealants, so both the tentative German recovery and the contested carbon-cost path bear directly on European supply and competitiveness. The output rebound is encouraging but fragile, and FEIQUE's verdict shows the ETS relief (see other insight in this alert) is seen as insufficient against the underlying cost gap. Treat the recovery as early and reversible, factor an unpredictable carbon-policy path into European site and investment decisions, and watch capacity utilisation and energy costs — not headline sales — as the real health signals.

Neue Zürcher Zeitung | FEIQUE | FEIQUE | Wirtschaftswoche | ChemEurope.com

item.title: USTR Jamieson Greer signalled 10–12.5% tariffs on around 60 countries to replace the 10% baseline expiring Friday, while Trump set phased 100% then 200% tariffs on generic drugs from 2028 — as Canada's 50% tariff moved into intensified talks.
item.description:
This is a new, wide-front escalation of trade policy rather than a single measure. With the Section 122 blanket 10% tariff — imposed after the Supreme Court struck down the "Liberation Day" regime — due to expire Friday, Greer said new duties of 10–12.5% will target around 60 economies including the EU, China, Japan, India, South Korea, Vietnam and Taiwan, nominally over forced-labour concerns, with separate excess-capacity investigations that could justify steeper duties later. Alongside, Trump announced a phased tariff on generic medicines under Section 232: zero for two years, then 100% from August 2028 and 200% from 2029 unless makers relocate production to the US — a direct hit to India, the largest generic exporter to America. The Canada front, delivered in the last alert as a signed 50% tariff on ~USD 20bn of goods, advanced to negotiation: Carney and Trump agreed to intensify talks before the duties take effect in 30 days, with Canada warning it is ready to retaliate. The common thread is a rebuilt, statute-hopping tariff architecture (Sections 122, 232, 301, 338) designed to survive legal challenge.

Industry Impact

For an ACS producer the near-term signal is that broad, layered tariffs are becoming the permanent backdrop for cross-border chemical and materials flows, not a one-off shock. A 10–12.5% duty across ~60 partners raises landed costs and invites retaliation that can catch chemical inputs; the generic-drug precedent shows how fast a sector can be singled out for reshoring pressure. Map exposure by trade lane and statute, model the Friday expiry and the phased pharma timeline for medical- and packaging-linked demand, and treat every current tariff exemption as provisional.

Les Echos | The Times of India | POLITICO | The Times of India | Financial Post

item.title: US forces launched a formal "Blockade 2.0" of Iran's ports with two carrier groups and over 20 warships as the Houthis declared a Red Sea blockade of Saudi Arabia, pushing Brent to a five-week high near USD 91 before it eased.
item.description:
The delta since the last alert is a shift from air campaign to a declared naval blockade plus a second maritime front. US Central Command completed a 10th consecutive night of strikes and mobilised the USS Abraham Lincoln and USS George H.W. Bush carrier strike groups and the USS Boxer amphibious group to blockade Iranian ports, disabling one merchant ship with kinetic weapons and firing a Hellfire missile at an empty tanker bound for Kharg Island. Iran's president declared "full-scale war". In parallel, the Iran-aligned Houthis' Red Sea blockade of Saudi Arabia turned real: two tankers of Saudi crude bound for China and India reversed course, threatening the Bab el-Mandeb route that Riyadh had been using to bypass Hormuz. Trump warned he would "take care of" the Houthis. Oil reflected the tension and the hesitation — Brent settled at USD 91.01 (+2%), a five-week high, then slipped toward USD 88.75 on trade and Fed-rate headlines. Analysts stress that commercial inventories and strategic reserves are far thinner than at the February onset, so any further deterioration transmits faster to price.

Industry Impact

For chemical and ACS producers the exposure widens with the second chokepoint: a Red Sea blockade on top of the Hormuz risk raises the tail risk to naphtha and feedstock freight even as spot crude wobbles on ceasefire and rate headlines. With buffers depleted, the next disruption feeds through to cost quickly and two-directionally. Keep hedging and freight-insurance contingency in place through the noise, treat both Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb as live scenarios, and plan H2 around elevated, spike-prone input costs rather than a return to pre-war normal.

Chinatimes | Handelsblatt | Al Jazeera | China Economic Net | The Economic Times

item.title: MIA Digest: The US-Iran war hardened into a two-carrier naval blockade and the Houthis opened a Red Sea front as oil neared USD 91; Washington launched a tariff blitz on ~60 countries and generic drugs; and Europe's chemical picture turned two-sided.
item.description:
• Iran war: two US carrier groups and 20+ warships now blockade Iran's ports, the Houthis opened a Red Sea front against Saudi Arabia, and oil hit a five-week high near USD 91 before easing.
  • Tariff blitz: Washington signalled 10-12.5% duties on ~60 countries to replace the expiring 10% baseline, plus phased 100-200% tariffs on generic drugs from 2028.
  • European chemicals: German chemical output is quietly recovering, but FEIQUE warned the EU's ETS revision could shrink industry, not emissions.
  • US-China tech: Washington weighs blacklisting Chinese AI labs while Beijing mulls AI and chip export controls, even as Wang Yi called China 'a partner, not a problem'.
  • Taiwan boom: June export orders hit USD 95.26bn (+59.4%) and think tanks now see 2026 growth above 10%.
